title: a text multiget's read buffer is copied after it went back to the rbuf cache
live_proof: the fix is an ancestor of the 1.6.45 tag: GitHub compare 1.6.45...7af02b0c87 reports status=behind, behind_by=566; the case reconstructs the pre-fix order of the two lines, which the commit's own diff shows
object: the connection's READ_BUFFER_SIZE read buffer, an object of the thread's rbuf cache (cache.c)
lifetime_ender: do_cache_free, which pushes the buffer on the cache's STAILQ (cache.c:135) and writes the list link into its first pointer-sized bytes; free() is never called
shape: stale object pointer / cache.c reuse / read through the dead pointer
allocator_layer: cache.c object cache over malloc, memcached 1.6.45
fidelity: model-consumer, real allocator: cache.c is upstream's file at the 1.6.45 pin through the port's two patches (freestanding shim, object lifetime hooks); the connection, the parser and the thread are reduced to the two lines the fix reorders, plus one prior buffer on the free list so the link read back is a pointer
layer_note: upstream's commit message names the mechanism -- the cache 'can reuse the first 8 bytes as a pointer to the internal freelist' -- and that is the only reason the defect was visible: for years the free list did not touch the buffer. The port's hook sits on that push, which is where the buffer's lifetime ends

native-fix-differential.oracle: the buggy arm copies the command after the buffer was pushed on the free list, so the copy's first bytes are the STAILQ link and differ from the command; the fixed arm copies first and the bytes are intact
native-fix-differential.note: unit_reissued is 1 in BOTH arms by design -- the next connection's cache_alloc pops the buffer either way; the arms differ only in whether the copy read it after the push

spatial.oracle: the sequence completes: report.completed == 1, no fault, the case marker printed
spatial.role: control for sublet: same binary and guest, one difference. An object keeps the alias it was carved with, so the freed buffer is readable and the copy proceeds -- with the link in it, as upstream saw

sublet.oracle: fault at the labelled read probe mc_defect_read, and nowhere else: exactly one fault, pc equal to the address the run's own marker published
sublet.note: the probe is the first read through rcurr after do_cache_free; the mark precedes it and nothing between them touches the buffer

poisoncap-spatial.requires: no CheriBSD or PoisonCap build of memcached's allocators exists

poisoncap-protected.requires: no CheriBSD or PoisonCap build of memcached's allocators exists

native-detect.requires: the buffer never reaches free(), so ASan has no event at the push; it would see the reuse only as an ordinary live object

status: native pair 2026-09-21 through the port, both arms as expected. Capstone domain 2026-09-21: spatial completes (completed=1, object_reuses=1), sublet faults at mc_defect_read cause=24 at the published address, 2 of 2 rounds; negative control fires. No poisoncap arm: no CheriBSD or PoisonCap build of memcached's allocators exists
note: damage is the copied command differing from what was read: natively the first 8 bytes become the free list's link, in a domain the first 16. Upstream reported an unhelpful ERROR to the client; this records the byte-level cause of it
